headline: Costa Rican colon reaches record high as US dollar drops to 444.45 colones
summary: The US dollar fell to a record low of 444.45 Costa Rican colones, extending its decline to 10.6% this year. Meanwhile, Vice President Francisco Gamboa took over the trade ministry while a 12.5% US tariff remains in place.
why: Exchange rate fluctuations impact foreign trade competitiveness, tourism revenue, and local purchasing power in Central America.

impacts.name: Costa Rican Colon
impacts.why: The local currency appreciated as the dollar fell to a record low exchange rate of 444.45 colones.
impacts.baseline_rule: first recorded price at or after created_at (15-minute price recorder); end = first price at least 24 h later, within 48 h

why_moved: Foreign exchange market dynamics pushed the dollar down 10.6% year-to-date against the colon.
